scenario: Constructed maintenance watch, unrelated to any Avalon or Jupiter Station episode
source_policy: All records below are synthetic. Branch shared is ancestral to both alpha and beta.

sources.author: Captain Vale
sources.text: Captain Vale selected manual inspection of the relay instead of a full reset, because resetting would erase anomaly evidence. The captain authorized this choice.

sources.author: Operations Clerk
sources.text: The first maintenance notice stated that Engineer Neri had until January 7, 2397, to finish the inspection.

sources.author: Captain Vale
sources.text: Correction to notice-1: the inspection deadline is January 6, 2397, not January 7. The earlier deadline remains in the archive as superseded.

sources.author: Engineering Registry
sources.text: Engineer Neri completed the relay inspection on January 5, 2397. Captain Vale acknowledged the report on January 6, 2397.

sources.author: Cadet Vale
sources.text: Cadet Vale wrote the maintenance comment from bridge-terminal-1. Captain Vale sometimes uses the same terminal, but did not write this entry.

sources.author: Engineer Neri
sources.text: Engineer Neri was the sole direct witness of the blue diagnostic pulse. No other firsthand witness is currently established.

sources.author: Assistant One
sources.text: This summary repeats source S06 from Engineer Neri. It is a derivative retelling, not an additional independent witness.

sources.author: Assistant Two
sources.text: This second summary also repeats S06 from Engineer Neri. It is not another independent witness.

sources.author: Sensor Officer
sources.text: The origin of the unexpected power spike is UNKNOWN. Available sensors did not establish a cause.

sources.author: Assistant One
sources.text: Assistant One suggested that the spike might be thermal. This remains speculation with no supporting sensor evidence and was never adopted.

sources.author: Engineer Neri
sources.text: In branch alpha, Engineer Neri sealed the auxiliary valve. This is a SIMULATED branch event and does not describe beta.

sources.author: Engineer Neri
sources.text: In branch beta, Engineer Neri left the auxiliary valve open. This is a SIMULATED branch event and does not describe alpha.

sources.author: Engineer Neri
sources.text: In alpha, after sealing the valve, Engineer Neri explicitly accepted the next commitment: calibrate the relay by January 8, 2397. It has not yet been reported complete.

sources.author: Engineer Neri
sources.text: In beta, after leaving the valve open, Engineer Neri declined to promise calibration until a safety review. The proposed follow-up has no accepted due date and no active commitment.

probes.question: What action was authorized, by whom, instead of which alternative, and why?
What was the original inspection deadline, the corrected deadline, and who corrected it?
When was the inspection completed, when acknowledged, and which came first?
Who wrote the comment from the shared bridge terminal, and which different person also used that terminal?
How many independent firsthand witnesses established the blue pulse, who was the origin, and are the AI summaries independent corroboration?
What caused the unexpected power spike?
What is the auxiliary valve state in alpha following the fork?
What is the auxiliary valve state in beta following the fork?
After the fork, what follow-up did Neri actually accept, and when is it due?
After the fork, did Neri accept the calibration commitment, and what is the next known prerequisite and due date?
